summary: June payrolls came in at just 57K, the weakest print in four months and well below forecasts of 110K. The Fed is now expected to take a patient approach rather than rush a rate hike decision, watching whether falling energy prices ease inflation. Separately, tariff uncertainty lingers as the temporary 10% blanket Section 122 surcharge faces a scheduled expiry on July 24, keeping corporate supply chain risk elevated.
tweet: Soft June payrolls (57K vs. 110K expected) have the Fed on hold watch, while a July 24 tariff cliff keeps supply chain risk alive — stocks greed, gold fear.
